# ProAgentStore

> Marketplace for server-powered AI agents. Creators publish agent templates; users subscribe and run private instances with their own state, knowledge, memory, and caller-owned AI credentials.

Primary site: https://proagentstore.online/
API: https://api.proagentstore.online/
MCP: https://mcp.proagentstore.online/mcp
MCP docs: https://proagentstore.online/docs/mcp/
MCP discovery: https://proagentstore.online/.well-known/mcp-server.json
GitHub marketplace repo: https://github.com/ProAgentStore/platform

## Skills

- [ProAgentStore Skills](https://proagentstore.online/skills/): public skill catalog and install instructions.
- [proagentstore-mcp-operator](https://proagentstore.online/skills/proagentstore-mcp-operator/): operate ProAgentStore account state only through MCP.
- [skills.json](https://proagentstore.online/skills.json): machine-readable skill metadata.

## Install

Direct MCP for Codex:

```bash
codex mcp add proagentstore --url https://mcp.proagentstore.online/mcp
codex mcp list
# If the server shows "Not logged in":
codex mcp login proagentstore
```

Direct MCP for Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http proagentstore https://mcp.proagentstore.online/mcp
claude mcp list
```

Local stdio proxy:

```bash
npx @proagentstore/cli mcp
```

Codex:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add ProAgentStore/platform
```

Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add ProAgentStore/platform
/plugin install proagentstore@proagentstore
/reload-plugins
```

## Correct MCP Runtime

Agents must use ProAgentStore account state only through the configured MCP server. Do not use the web UI or private REST/API routes unless the user explicitly overrides this rule.

MCP safety:

- OAuth scopes: `read`, `write`, `runtime`, `destructive`. A plain browser sign-in grants `read write runtime` — `destructive` is never a default and must be requested explicitly at authorization time.
- Server-side read-only mode: `MCP_READ_ONLY=1`.
- Use `dry_run: true` on mutating tools before making uncertain changes.
- Thirteen tools require an exact `confirm` value, compared with `===`. In twelve cases the value is the tool's own name: `write_agent_file`, `batch_write_agent_files`, `unregister_instance_runtime`, `cancel_instance_task`, `cancel_instance`, `delete_instance_knowledge`, `delete_instance_memory`, `delete_instance_file`, `delete_instance_trigger`, `delete_instance_connector_grant`, `delete_supervision`, `clear_instance_messages`. The exception is `remove_repo`, which takes `confirm: "remove_all_repos"` and only when removing every repo.
- The tool list is per-connection: some tools are gated to the console surfaces of the agents you actually subscribe to (`apply`, `repo`, `coding`). Call `tools/list` — a missing tool usually means a missing subscription, not an outage.
- Failures do not set `isError`. A failed call returns text beginning `Error: `, or JSON carrying an `error` key.
- Use `mcp_audit_log` to inspect recent write, runtime, dry-run, denied, and destructive MCP events.

Use public trial chat only for discovery:

```text
list_agents -> chat_with_agent
```

Use private instance chat for real user work:

```text
list_agents -> subscribe_agent -> my_instances -> add_instance_knowledge -> chat_with_instance -> instance_messages
```

If `chat_with_instance` says it needs a Cloudflare Workers AI account ID and API token, the private runtime is working and correctly waiting for caller-owned AI credentials.

Browser-capable agents split the work: PAGS runs the control-plane brain (a durable Cloudflare Workflow using the caller's BYOK Claude) and the local ProAgentStore browser runtime is the hands (real Chrome via Playwright, driven by ARIA snapshot + act — act by role and accessible name, no CSS selectors). Start it with `pags up`, which connects outbound over a WebSocket relay (no tunnel binary, no inbound port) and serves every active agent whose capabilities declare a local runtime — attaching newly eligible ones while it runs, so a restart is not needed. There is no `--tunnel` flag in the current CLI. The job-apply brain fills and submits real applications, pausing for one of three human handoffs — captcha, stuck, or needs_input — resolved in a single live takeover, with a per-ATS learned-tips cache and "Open in Gmail" confirmation-email links.

Platform features: a single unified work board per instance (runtime tasks + application records), the LLM-driven job-apply agent, Coder (drive Claude Code / Codex / Gemini / Grok on any GitHub repo via a local runner), Repo Chat (read-only server-side repo ingest + RAG), voice chat (speech in/out), and observability via the `list_errors` MCP tool.
